verdicts.reason: A breaks the reading order: the CTA pill sits alone in the top-left corner above the headline, leaving a dead orange band below it. The headline is shrunk and wraps awkwardly ('and a / little sunshine'), and the subline is jammed right under it with no gap. B keeps the original centred order and gives the headline real presence, but the italic subline is set almost as large as the headline, so the two compete. B's CTA is also shrunk to a tiny pill with nearly illegible text, stranded at the bottom after a large empty gap.
